concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor conceded the disclosure gap remains open and supplied no new admissible evidence of final model-card or equivalent launch disclosure.
The Actor conceded the available risk acceptance is only a draft, unapproved, and does not address the exposed use case. No new approval evidence was provided.
The Actor conceded the rollout gate does not exclude the cybersecurity alert triage segment from the initial cohort. No new operational exclusion evidence was provided.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence; the response narrows and reframes the claim using the same record. That reframing is analytically cleaner, but it does not satisfy the controlling policy predicate. The admissible evidence still shows: the affected cybersecurity alert triage use case remains below target and exposed in the initial rollout cohort; the policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch; the available risk acceptance is only a draft with no approver and does not address this exposure; and rollout controls do not cure disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. Aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, rollback capability, and monitoring support a narrower claim about operational launch readiness, but they do not convert the record into compliant certification. This is the distinction between a caveated business or readiness narrative and an unresolved compliance predicate. Because the predicate remains unmet on the available evidence, the final outcome remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the material limitation for cybersecurity alert triage was disclosed before launch.
No approved risk acceptance covers the exposed cybersecurity alert triage weakness.
The rollout mitigation does not exclude the affected use case from exposure, so rollout controls do not satisfy the policy predicate.
